Review Cloudflare Workers?

Reviewers are overwhelmingly positive, mostly founders describing Cloudflare Workers as a fast, low-maintenance way to run global backends at the edge. They repeatedly praise simple deployment, no server management, no cold starts, and a generous free tier. Technical users also like how Workers bundles compute with services such as D1, KV, R2, Vectorize, Durable Objects, and AI tooling, which reduces vendor sprawl. A few maker reviews note limits shaping architecture, but direct end-user feedback is largely absent, so this view is mostly builder-led.

Review Cloudflare?

Reviewers mostly see Cloudflare as dependable infrastructure for speed, security, and DNS, with quick setup and easier site management showing up again and again. Users especially praise CDN performance, DDoS protection, caching, and long-term reliability, though several note a steep learning curve and some complexity in advanced settings. Founder feedback from the makers of daily.dev, Magic Patterns, and Inworld adds that Workers and related tools are low-cost, globally fast, and simple to deploy, but one founder said bot protection diagnostics were hard to trace when legitimate traffic was blocked.

Review Cloudflare Pages?

Reviewers describe Cloudflare Pages as a fast, reliable, low-friction way to host static sites and frontend apps, with especially strong Git integration, automatic builds, quick global deploys, preview links, and useful extras from the wider Cloudflare stack such as DNS, redirects, security, and lightweight backend functions. Founders behind products like SKI and Tucky mainly cite it as practical infrastructure for websites and downloads. The main criticism is narrower: when deployments fail, the dashboard, debugging, and environment settings can be unclear.
